Federal taxable income = 80,000.00 - 15,750.00 federal standard deduction = 64,250.00 (the federal senior deduction is ignored). Form 40 (filing status married filing separately): line 7 federal AGI 80,000.00. Line 8 additions 0.00; line 9 = 80,000.00 + 0.00 = 80,000.00. Form 39R Part B line 7 Social Security and railroad benefits included in federal income = 0.00 + 0.00 = 0.00. Line 8 retirement benefits deduction: line 8a 48,216.00 (the booklet prints no figure for married filing separately, so the projection's fallback (single); the 'can't file separately' bar is in Part One, for all other retirees, not for service members); line 8b railroad benefits received 0.00; line 8c Social Security received (gross, both spouses, Box 5) 0.00; line 8d = 48,216.00 - 0.00 - 0.00, not below zero, = 48,216.00; line 8e (person 0 age 63: 60,000.00 qualifies, age 62 or older) = 60,000.00; line 8f smaller of 8d and 8e = 48,216.00. Line 18 health insurance premiums: none in the inputs, 0.00. Line 24 total subtractions = 0.00 + 48,216.00 = 48,216.00. Form 40 line 10 48,216.00; line 11 total adjusted income = 80,000.00 - 48,216.00 = 31,784.00. Line 12a boxes checked 0. Standard Deduction Worksheet: line 1 15,750.00; line 4 15,750.00; line 5 0 x 1,600.00 = 0.00; line 6 15,750.00. Line 15 0.00 (no Schedule A); line 16 15,750.00. Line 17 = 31,784.00 - 15,750.00 = 16,034.00. Line 18 federal Form 1040 lines 13a and 13b taken as 0.00; line 19 Idaho taxable income 16,034.00. Line 20 worksheet: line 1 16,034.00; line 2 4,811.00; line 3 = 11,223.00; line 4 at 5.3%; line 5 tax = 11,223.00 x 5.3% = 594.819, to the cent 594.82 (the return rounds to whole dollars, PDF p.8, and shows 595; expected keeps the formula). Lines 21-24 credits 0.00; line 25 0.00; line 26 594.82. Food Tax Credit Worksheet (Form 40 line 43): 1 x 155.00 = 155.00. State income tax = 594.82 - 155.00 = 439.82. Line 31 Permanent Building Fund tax 10.00 is on the return but the projection does not charge it (approximations).
accepted_approximations: The retirement maximum prints for single and joint only. A head of household, qualifying surviving spouse or married filing separately return has no printed figure; the projection gives only the two printed amounts, so such a return needs the fallback a status not given takes for brackets (single; joint for a qualifying surviving spouse).
The Permanent Building Fund tax of 10 a return (Form 40 line 31) is not charged.
